The tests you write must be hermetic (no live Worker) and few but complete: add a test only when it covers something useful in full, and update or delete existing tests whose old behaviour you are deliberately changing.

FILES YOU OWN (edit only these two): /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge/scripts/ringer/environment_narration/hidden_bench_prose_probe.py and /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge/tests/test_hidden_bench_prose_probe.py. You may READ anything. NEVER modify anything under bench/results/, data/stories/, storygame/, docs/ or .plans/.

BACKGROUND. `hidden_bench_prose_probe.py` ran a billed 60-call prose probe (stage 2) whose recorded result is FAIL and must stay reproducible. Review found its measurement flawed in four ways. (a) `_capture_package` adds a `LEGACY VISIBLE BENCH OBJECTS:` block to the P0 opening and pre-find prompts after capture, so P0 is not the real old-package request. (b) It builds a bare `CloudflareTurnProvider`, so no payload contains the `THINGS:` block that the hosted game renders through `storygame.runtime.item_facts.ItemFactsProvider`. (c) The raw model reply is scored alone, although the game appends a package-authored delivery segment (for the P1 find: "Kristin reaches beneath the park bench. She retrieves a transit token, a handwritten number sequence and Michelle's photograph. She keeps all three with her."); `CloudflareTurnProvider._compose_authored_handoff` and `_compose_staged_cue` in storygame/runtime/cloudflare.py do that appending. (d) The blind key is only checked by row count. Do the following. Frozen gate logic must NOT change: leave LABEL_NAMES, P1A_BAD_LABELS, report(), write_label_freeze, _freeze_hash, the label-hash check and the PASS/FAIL arithmetic exactly as they are.

1. REMOVE the P0-only augmentation in `_capture_package` entirely (the block that appends `LEGACY VISIBLE BENCH OBJECTS:` and the three names). The P0 arm is then the untouched request the HEAD package really produces. Replace the test `test_head_control_retains_the_old_clue_names` with one that asserts the P0 opening/pre-find payload text contains no injected block, i.e. equals what the real provider rendered.

2. CAPTURE THROUGH THE WORLD-AWARE PROVIDER. Build the provider the way the hosted game builds it, not by hand-assembling a visible-thing list. Look at how storygame/web_demo.py and bench/core.py (`prompt_for`) construct `ItemFactsProvider` (arguments item_facts, mode, state_axes, seed_from_package, drop_rules, held_by, mark_fixed) and follow the hosted game's choice. Keep `_request` stubbed so capture stays hermetic with no HTTP. The stub reply must satisfy whatever the provider validates (the reply may need an `item_facts` key; make the stub minimal but valid). After the change at least one captured payload must contain a `THINGS:` block, and the hidden bench clues must not appear in the P1 opening and pre-find prompts (the existing `preflight` terms check must still pass for the P1 arm). Do NOT inject, edit or filter any prompt text yourself.

3. RECORD COMPOSITION SEPARATELY. Each captured payload gets a new key `composed_segments`: the list of {"kind", "text"} dicts for the segments the real engine/provider path produced after composition for that turn (the stubbed narration segment plus any appended package delivery or staged cue segment). Obtain them from the real runtime path (the accepted proposal / engine result), never by scanning prompt text. The raw `system` and `user` request text stays untouched. The P1 find payload's composed_segments must contain the authored delivery text above; every payload must have the key (an empty list if nothing was appended is fine for the others).

4. ADD MODE `--composed-view`: `--composed-view --rows ROWS.json --out DIR`. It reads an existing rows.json READ-ONLY and writes two files into DIR: `raw_view.md` and `composed_view.md`. Both show every row as a section headed `## sample-NNN` using the SAME shuffle (SHUFFLE_SEED) and opaque ids as `sheets()` so the ids line up with the existing blind_key.json, and each section shows only `State:`, `Sample:` and the text, never the arm and never the payload id (no line may start with `Arm:` or `Payload:`). raw_view shows the model reply text as `sheets()` does. composed_view shows, for every row, the reply text followed by the authored delivery segment for that state: obtain the delivery by running the real composition helper (`_compose_authored_handoff` or `_compose_staged_cue`) on a provider built over the scene 1B state for that row's state, with the reply parsed through the typed `TurnProposal` model (json.loads then validation; no text scraping). If a reply cannot be validated as a TurnProposal, show it unchanged and mark that section `not composable`. Engine text and narrator text must stay visibly separate within a section (for example a labelled `Narrator:` and `Engine (appended by the game):` part). The first lines of composed_view.md must state that it is a post hoc, inferred composition, not accepted game turns, and that it does not change the recorded stage 2 FAIL. Add the mode to the parser's mutually exclusive group and `main`. It must not write into the rows' own directory unless `--out` says so, and must never alter the input file. Cost is zero.

5. ADD A BLIND-KEY BIJECTION TEST: a helper and test asserting that, for a key and its rows, the set of key `row_index` values is exactly 1..len(rows) with no duplicates, and that each key entry's payload_id, arm, state and sample equal those of the row at that index. Apply it to the output of `sheets()` on a synthetic complete rows file, AND to the checked-in frozen files (read-only) `bench/results/environment-narration/t9h-hidden/prose/rows.json` with `.../prose/sheets.md/blind_key.json`. Add a test for the composed view over synthetic rows (60 sections, no arm lines, delivery present for find rows, post hoc header). Keep the existing budget, missing-label, hash-tamper and no-replacement (429) tests; update any that your change legitimately breaks.

HOW TO VERIFY BEFORE YOU FINISH: run the check yourself with `bash /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge/scripts/ringer/environment_narration/check_t9h_stage2_measure_repair.sh`. It verifies frozen artifacts are byte-identical, tests, ruff, the capture content, both views over the frozen rows, and that the frozen report still reproduces. Do not edit the check. When done, print a short summary: what you changed, which provider construction you copied and from where, and anything in the plan you could not do.
